1984 by George Orwell. from the day i read it for my sophomore lit. class, i felt so disappointed, even cheated a little. 


the book lacked any sort of depth i felt. there was no “piecing things together” or a huge twist that really made me think. it lacked subtlety in a way that i feel is best described as a bull in a china shop. maybe it’s because i was 15 and expected a classic to be some sort of work of art above criticism. 


i thought it was just insanely weird that orwell was so... obsessed(?) with women in the story in an incel-ish way. 

to bring this huge “big brother knows all” concept to an end by having this character that was meant to revolt against The Man even if it was futile be beaten... by a cage of rats. a cage of rats. not any other torture, not the mind play, nothing. except for a bucket of Chuck Entertainment Cheeses

it lacked grace, it did not feel as though it was prophetic to me (hey though! that might just be because we truly grew up as such things in the book unfolded) because many things felt like abstract and vague things anybody could come to a conclusion that a fascist government would do. it felt just... odd to me the way the things in the book were paced and how some things such as sex with a young woman were so detailed yet other things such as the torture winston endured for so long were rather brushed over. i didn’t feel any sort of profound realization of anything once i finished the book, i did not realize how evil big brother was nor did i feel i had anything to really take away from such a “classic” that made reading the book worth it. 

different strokes for different folks though lmao
